clips.title: Top 3 Things You Should Know About Webhooks!
clips.why: A clear picture of the two ways to learn about a change: ask again and again (polling), or be called (a webhook).
look: What polling costs: many requests that find nothing new, and a delay between the change and the next poll.
What a webhook needs: a URL the other service can call. For us that would be a door from the internet into the orchestrator.
clips.after: We accept polling's costs, one request a minute and up to a minute of delay, to keep that door closed.

clips.title: Webhooks for Beginners – From Polling to Real‑Time Events
clips.why: What a team takes on when it receives webhooks: proving each call is real, and not losing events when the receiver is down.
look: Every webhook call must be checked, because anyone on the internet can send a request to the URL.
What happens to events that arrive while the receiver is down.
clips.after: With polling we have neither problem: nobody can call us, and a poll after an outage simply finds every ticket that is assigned now.

clips.title: Simple Local Dev Environments & New Scheduled Workflows
clips.why: The Temporal team presents Schedules, the feature our poll is built on, which replaced an older cron option on workflows.
look: A schedule is its own object in Temporal, with an ID you can list, describe, pause and update.
Listen for the policies: what happens when the previous run is still going, and what happens to times that were missed.
clips.after: poll-jira-nova is one of these objects: every minute, overlap SKIP, and a catch-up window of one minute.

clips.title: Kubernetes CronJobs in 8 Minutes! Schedule and Automate Like a Pro
clips.why: Kubernetes CronJobs face the same question as our schedule, a new tick while the last job is still running, and give it the same three answers.
look: Allow, Forbid and Replace: compare them with ALLOW_ALL, SKIP and TERMINATE_OTHER.
Which choice would you pick for a job that asks a slow service for news?
clips.after: Forbid is Kubernetes' name for what our schedules call SKIP: a slow poll never gets a second copy of itself.

practice.q: Jira is slow and every search takes longer than the interval. Which overlap policy keeps Jira from getting more requests exactly when it is struggling?

options.why: A tick that comes while a poll runs starts nothing, so there is never more than one poll at a time.
Every tick starts a new poll, so slow polls overlap and the slow Jira gets even more requests.
It never runs two at once, but it keeps every missed tick and runs them all, one after the other, long after they are useful.

practice.q: Finish the policies of poll-jira-nova so a slow poll never gets a second copy.
practice.hint: Four letters: the tick is dropped.
practice.why: SKIP drops a tick while the last poll still runs. The next poll finds the same tickets, so nothing is lost.

practice.q: ensureSchedules runs at every worker start. Which error does create throw when the schedule exists already?
practice.hint: The schedule is already there and running.
practice.why: That error is expected on every start after the first. The code catches only that one and updates the schedule instead.

practice.q: You assign RH-1234 to Nova at 09:00:20. Put what happens in order.
items: At 09:01:00 the schedule poll-jira-nova ticks and starts pollJira on the orchestrator's queue
startMatches asks Jira for tickets assigned to Nova and finds RH-1234
startRun starts nova:RH-1234, because no run with that name is open
At 09:02:00 the next poll finds RH-1234 again
startRun joins the open run nova:RH-1234, so there is still one run
practice.why: The schedule only starts polls. The workflow ID, with the conflict policy that joins the open run, is what keeps one run per ticket.

practice.q: Read the cron expression of one of our routines: "41 6 * * 1" in Asia/Jerusalem. When does it run?

options.why: Minute 41, hour 6, any day of the month, any month, day of the week 1, which is Monday (0 is Sunday).

options.text: At 04:16 on the first day of every month
options.why: The first field is the minute and the second the hour. The 1 is in the day-of-week field, not the day of the month.
That would need a step like */41. A plain 41 means minute 41 of the hour.
